BiblicalUsage: Tartan is not a man's name but a title, the commander-in-chief of the Assyrian army. The king of Assyria sent Tartan and Rabsaris and Rabshakeh to Hezekiah at Jerusalem, and in the year that Tartan came unto Ashdod and fought against it, Isaiah was told to walk naked and barefoot as a sign.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the title matters more than the man: the Assyrian commander is named by his office, and his office could not stand against the Lord.
